name: Ghidra - Software Reverse Engineering Suite
description: Ghidra is the NSA's open-source reverse-engineering suite: a multi-architecture disassembler and decompiler with scripting, cross-references, data-type management, and version tracking. Used to understand closed-source binaries, find vulnerabilities, recover algorithms/keys, and triage malware without executing it.
notes:
=== LAUNCH ===
  ghidraRun            # GUI (needs JDK 17+)

=== WORKFLOW ===
  1. Create a project -> import the target binary (auto-detects arch/format)
  2. Let auto-analysis run (functions, xrefs, strings, data types)
  3. CodeBrowser: use the Decompiler (right pane) for C-like pseudocode
  4. 'g' to goto address; 'x' for cross-references; L to rename; ; to comment
  5. Window > Defined Strings / Symbol Tree / Function Graph

=== FIND VULNS / SECRETS ===
  - Search > For Strings; look for format strings, system(), strcpy, memcpy
  - Decompiler for logic around input parsing / auth checks
  - Symbol Tree -> imports (dangerous APIs)

=== HEADLESS / SCRIPTING ===
  analyzeHeadless <proj_dir> <proj> -import <file> -postScript <script.py>
  # Python (Jython) or Java scripts; GhidraScript API

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  IDA Pro / IDA Free    # industry standard disassembler
  radare2 / rizin       # CLI RE framework
  Binary Ninja          # commercial
  x64dbg / gdb          # dynamic debugging

recommended.note: IDA-based code analysis as an alternative disassembler.
radare2 for CLI-driven RE and scripting.
Static triage workflow for Linux binaries.

defense.why_it_works: Compiled binaries retain enough structure (imports, strings, control flow) for a decompiler to recover high-level logic. Without obfuscation or anti-analysis, secrets, algorithms, and vulnerable patterns are fully recoverable from a shipped binary.
defense.prerequisites: A copy of the target binary. No execution required; analysis is fully offline on the analyst's machine.
defense.impact: Recovery of proprietary logic, hardcoded keys/credentials, license checks, and discovery of exploitable bugs - all without source code.
defense.detection: Not detectable on the defender side (offline analysis of a distributed binary). Defense is anti-RE hardening of the binary itself, not telemetry.
defense.artifacts: None on the target environment; the analysis happens on the attacker's workstation.
defense.prevention: Do not embed secrets in binaries (use runtime secret retrieval); strip symbols; apply obfuscation/packing and anti-debug/anti-tamper for sensitive code; server-side enforcement of license/auth logic so client reversing yields nothing of value; code signing to detect tampering.
